𖿢:
{{also|𠃊|ㆹ|L|ℓ|ㄴ|𠃋|ო|uni=auto}}
{{character info}}

==Chinese==

===Alternative forms===
The appearance of this letter varies widely between different texts or fonts. The most common form is as a vertical and horizontal line. It also varies which one of the lines is longer. Its standardized version in the official Unicode chart is with horizontal line longer, however that is mostly due to the fact that before it’s encoding, {{codepoint|ㄴ}} was used, but in the original writing, it could also exist with the vertical line longer. Additionally, the bottom was usually thicker.

There also exist forms with slightly slanted vertical line, appearing similar to {{l|mul|𠃋}}, however those are not so common.

===Punctuation mark===
{{head|zh|punctuation mark}}

# Mark, called "hook" or "tadpole" mark, or {{zh-l|鉤識號}} in Chinese that denotes pause or break in the text. ''(See usage notes)''

====Usage notes====
The usage of the mark varies greatly between the texts. They can be used only to mark the end of a section or as frequently as to mark the end of a clause.
𖿣:
{{also|々|〻|Appendix:Variations of "="}}
{{character info}}
==Chinese==

===Alternative forms===
In vertical layout, the character may appear as two short lines or as two dots in the upper right corner, however the latter is mostly limited to {{zh-l|楷體}} fonts. In later adopted horizontal layout, the character only rarely appears, and looks similar to an equals sign ({{l|mul|=}}) with the lower stroke at the baseline or the character is centered in the middle.

===Glyph origin===
{{rfe|zh|From 𠄞 (ancient form of 上)?}}

===Iteration mark===
{{head|zh|iteration mark}}

# Indicates repetition of character. ''(see usage notes)''

====Usage notes====
The character is used very similarly to modern iteration marks ({{l|zh|々}}, {{l|zh|〻}}).

The character signifies repetition of the previous character, but if two marks are placed with only one character in between, the sequence of both characters is repeated:

* {{lang|zh|水𖿣}} would nowadays be usually written as {{l|zh|水水|tr=-}}.
* {{lang|zh|玄𖿣牝𖿣}} would nowadays be usually written as {{l|zh|[[玄牝]][[玄牝]]|tr=-}}.

In vertical layouts, the older texts tend to position it as a smaller character in the space between other characters, but modern practice is to render it as a full-sized character. In the modern-day, its use is primarily limited to {{l|en|palaeography}}.
